<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">                             # no tools line: whatever the level that opened it has</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>In the test, <code>tools: [Read]</code> told to run <code>echo HELLO</code> called no tool at all and only answered <code>I don't have access to a Bash tool.</code>; with <code>Bash</code> added to the list it came back with <code>HELLO</code>.</p>
<p>MCP tools work the same way: if they are not listed in <code>tools</code>, the subagent does not get them. Tested with a GitHub MCP server attached:</p>





















<table><thead><tr><th><code>tools</code> says</th><th>MCP tools the subagent gets</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>[Read]</code></td><td>none</td></tr><tr><td><code>[Read, mcp__github__search_repositories]</code></td><td>only that one, and it can be called as usual</td></tr><tr><td>no <code>tools</code> line</td><td>all 26 tools of the GitHub server</td></tr></tbody></table>
<h4>Does <code>skills</code> let the subagent use skills?</h4>
<p>No. Write <code>skills: [inner]</code> and the engine pastes <code>inner</code>'s body into the subagent's conversation at the start, but no <code>Skill</code> appears on the tool list:</p>
<pre><code>system prompt: You are a test agent. ...
the full SKILL.md of inner   ← pasted in by the engine
tool list: Read              ← no Skill
</code></pre>
<p>In other words, the subagent knows what kind of skill <code>inner</code> is and what it does, but has no <code>Skill</code> ability. In the test it reported having only <code>Read</code>, yet could say what <code>inner</code> asks for.</p>
<p>For a subagent to call skills, put <code>Skill</code> in <code>tools</code>, or leave the line out. Yet the SDK's type file <code>sdk.d.ts</code> marks <code>tools: [..., Skill]</code> as deprecated and tells you to write <code>skills</code> instead of declaring it in <code>tools</code>; read that literally, and the subagent can no longer call skills. I find this part pretty misleading.</p>
<h4>The SDK's <code>query()</code></h4>
<p>The SDK has no definition file; the same fields go straight into <code>query()</code>:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">query</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">({ prompt: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"..."</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, options: { tools: [</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Read"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Bash"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">], skills: [</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"inner"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">] } })</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>But <code>tools</code> and <code>skills</code> mean something different there:</p>






























<table><thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>agent definition</th><th><code>query()</code></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>tools</code></td><td>replaces the whole list; MCP tools not declared there are left out</td><td>replaces built-in tools only, MCP tools stay</td></tr><tr><td><code>skills</code></td><td>the subagent gets these skills' full text at the start, which has nothing to do with whether it can call <code>Skill</code></td><td>pastes nothing, <code>Skill</code> can call only the listed ones</td></tr><tr><td><code>disallowedTools</code></td><td>removes the listed tools</td><td>same</td></tr><tr><td><code>allowedTools</code></td><td>no such field</td><td>listed tools run without asking the user</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>With <code>skills: ["inner"]</code> in <code>query()</code>, asking the model to run <code>outer</code> and then <code>inner</code> gave (SDK 0.3.302):</p>
<pre><code>Skill {"skill":"outer"}  →  Skill outer is not in this session's skills allowlist
Skill {"skill":"inner"}  →  Launching skill: inner
</code></pre>
<h3>hook</h3>
<p>A hook is a rule the engine runs automatically at a fixed moment, written in <code>settings.json</code>. For example, every time the model calls <code>Write</code> or <code>Edit</code>, the engine first runs a check script:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{ </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"PreToolUse"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"matcher"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Write|Edit"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">    "hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [{ </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"type"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"bash ~/hooks/prose-guard.sh"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> }] }</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">] } }</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p><code>PreToolUse</code> is the event: it fires before a tool runs and can deny that tool call; the <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks">official reference</a> lists 33 events in all. <code>matcher</code> is compared against the tool name. The inner <code>hooks</code> array holds what runs on a match, called the action from here on.</p>
<p><strong>The engine runs the action; the main-line model takes no part.</strong> There are five types:</p>



































<table><thead><tr><th>type</th><th>how it is written</th><th>what the engine does</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>command</code></td><td><code>{"type": "command", "command": "bash check.sh"}</code></td><td>starts a process, hook input on stdin</td></tr><tr><td><code>prompt</code></td><td><code>{"type": "prompt", "prompt": "Is this safe? $ARGUMENTS"}</code></td><td>makes one extra call to a small model</td></tr><tr><td><code>agent</code></td><td><code>{"type": "agent", "prompt": "... $ARGUMENTS"}</code></td><td>opens a subagent to decide, Haiku unless <code>model</code> is set</td></tr><tr><td><code>mcp_tool</code></td><td><code>{"type": "mcp_tool", "server": "marker", "tool": "record"}</code></td><td>sends <code>tools/call</code> straight to that MCP server</td></tr><tr><td><code>http</code></td><td>not tested</td><td>POSTs the hook input to a URL</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><code>$ARGUMENTS</code> is replaced with the hook input. Of the five, only <code>mcp_tool</code> actually calls a tool (<code>marker</code> is a test MCP server I set up); none of the other four leaves a <code>tool_use</code> in the log.</p>
<p>A matcher made only of letters, digits, <code>_</code>, <code>-</code>, spaces, <code>,</code> and <code>|</code> is an exact match; any other character makes it a regex:</p>








































<table><thead><tr><th>matcher</th><th>how it compares</th><th>which tools match</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>Bash</code></td><td>exact</td><td>Bash only</td></tr><tr><td><code>Write|Edit</code></td><td>exact</td><td>Write, Edit</td></tr><tr><td><code>Write, Edit</code></td><td>exact</td><td>Write, Edit</td></tr><tr><td><code>mcp__jira</code></td><td>exact</td><td>none</td></tr><tr><td><code>mcp__jira__.*</code></td><td>regex</td><td>every tool on the jira server</td></tr><tr><td>empty or <code>*</code></td><td>everything</td><td>every tool</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>If the regex is broken, say <code>Bash(</code> with no closing parenthesis, the engine does not stop; it only prints <code>Invalid regex pattern in hook matcher</code> and counts it as no match. Opening a subagent is a call to <code>Agent</code>, so to do something before every subagent launch, put <code>Agent</code> in the matcher.</p>
<h2>The sixteen combinations</h2>
<p>Each row below is one "who calls whom". The middle column says who actually issues the call, and after the arrow is the field that makes it work. The agent rows mean the subagent a <code>.claude/agents/&#x3C;name>.md</code> opens.</p>
<p>The callers fall into four groups:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>model</strong> (4 rows): the call happens only when the model writes a <code>tool_use</code>. If a subagent's <code>tools:</code> includes <code>Agent</code>, the model has <code>Agent</code> available, but the model decides whether to call it. The "skill calls tool" row also counts as model, because the model sends Bash on the skill body's instruction; <code>allowed-tools: Read</code> does not stop it</li>
<li><strong>engine</strong> (5 rows): the field names what to call, and the engine does it without the model. If a skill sets <code>context: fork</code>, the engine opens a subagent to run it; if a hook has an <code>mcp_tool</code> action, the engine calls that MCP tool itself. <code>hooks:</code> appears in two rows, "subagent calls hook" and "skill calls hook", so four fields map to five rows</li>
<li><strong>indirect</strong> (3 rows): no field at all; the request goes into the conversation as text, and the model may or may not act on it</li>
<li><strong>not possible</strong> (4 rows): a tool has no config of its own, so there is nowhere to say what it should call</li>
</ul>


























































































<table><thead><tr><th>Caller and target</th><th>Issued by</th><th>What came back</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>subagent calls subagent</td><td>model ← <code>tools:</code> including <code>Agent</code></td><td>the second-level <code>tool_use</code> carries the first level's <code>parent_tool_use_id</code></td></tr><tr><td>subagent calls hook</td><td>engine ← frontmatter <code>hooks:</code></td><td>returns <code>BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK</code> (the folder must be trusted)</td></tr><tr><td>subagent calls tool</td><td>model ← <code>tools:</code></td><td>leave it out and it matches the parent; <code>tools: [Read]</code> leaves it with Read only</td></tr><tr><td>subagent calls skill</td><td>model ← <code>tools:</code> including <code>Skill</code>, or no <code>tools:</code> line</td><td>a <code>tool_use</code> named <code>Skill</code>, whose <code>parent_tool_use_id</code> points at the first level</td></tr><tr><td>hook calls subagent</td><td>engine ← an <code>agent</code> action</td><td><code>Agent hook condition was not met: AGENT-HOOK-BLOCKED</code></td></tr><tr><td><strong>hook calls hook</strong></td><td>indirect model ← no field</td><td>the model inside an <code>agent</code> action calls a tool, which fires it again</td></tr><tr><td>hook calls tool</td><td>engine ← an <code>mcp_tool</code> action</td><td>the MCP server receives the <code>tools/call</code>, with no <code>tool_use</code> in the log</td></tr><tr><td><strong>hook calls skill</strong></td><td>indirect model ← no field</td><td><code>additionalContext</code> asks the model to call it, ends at <code>GREET-RAN</code></td></tr><tr><td>skill calls subagent</td><td>engine ← <code>context: fork</code></td><td><code>Skill "forktest" completed (forked execution).</code></td></tr><tr><td>skill calls hook</td><td>engine ← frontmatter <code>hooks:</code></td><td>returns <code>BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK</code></td></tr><tr><td>skill calls tool</td><td>model ← <code>allowed-tools</code> does not restrict</td><td><code>allowed-tools: Read</code> is declared and the body still gets Bash</td></tr><tr><td><strong>skill calls skill</strong></td><td>indirect model ← no field</td><td>the body asks the model to call it, returns <code>INNER-RAN</code></td></tr><tr><td>tool calls subagent</td><td>not possible</td><td>no such path in the engine</td></tr><tr><td>tool calls skill</td><td>not possible</td><td>no such path in the engine</td></tr><tr><td>tool calls tool</td><td>not possible</td><td>no such path in the engine</td></tr><tr><td>tool calls hook</td><td>not possible</td><td>the engine calls the hook around the tool; the tool takes no part</td></tr></tbody></table>
<h3>How deep can subagents nest?</h3>
<p>A subagent can open another subagent, up to a ceiling. Levels count like this:</p>
<pre><code>main line (level 0)
└─ subagent A (level 1)
   └─ subagent B (level 2)
</code></pre>
<p>The default ceiling inside the binary is 3, but the engine also reads a remote flag that overrides it, so the actual ceiling is not necessarily 3. To set it yourself, pass an environment variable at startup:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">=</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">2</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1"> claude</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5"> -p</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> "..."</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>Set it to 2 and the main line opens A (depth 1) and A opens B (depth 2), both fine. When B goes to open a third level, its tool list has no <code>Agent</code>. Set it to 1 and it is A's list that is missing it.</p>
<p>B's own definition does list <code>Agent</code>:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="yaml" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="yaml" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">name</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">nb</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">description</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">nesting test agent level B</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">tools</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Read</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Bash</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Agent</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">]</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">---</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>But B is already at level 2, the ceiling, so the tool list the engine hands to it has no <code>Agent</code>, and the <code>Agent</code> in the definition file has no effect.</p>
<h3>Can a tool call anything itself?</h3>
<p>tool calls subagent, tool calls skill, tool calls tool: none of these three holds. When a tool is called it does one thing with its arguments and calls nothing else.</p>
<p><code>Agent</code> is no exception. The subagent it opens goes on to call tools, skills and further subagents, but those calls are all issued by the model inside the subagent; <code>Agent</code> only opens the subagent.</p>
<p>An MCP server you write yourself can, on receiving <code>tools/call</code>, start a separate <code>claude</code> process in its own code, and that process can open subagents and run skills. But that is a different session, so it does not count as a tool in this session calling anything.</p>
<p><code>tool calls hook</code> does not hold either. The hook does run, but it runs before Bash starts, the engine calls it, and Bash takes no part from start to finish:</p>
<pre><code>model writes a tool_use, name=Bash, command=echo MAIN
→ engine checks the hook settings in settings.json
→ the matcher hits, the engine runs that action and waits for it to finish
→ deny     → it stops here, the shell never receives anything
→ no deny  → only now does the engine hand echo MAIN to a shell
</code></pre>
<p>When the hook runs, Bash has not even started, so Bash cannot be what triggered it. <code>PostToolUse</code> also waits for Bash to finish, and then the engine runs the hook.</p>
<h3>Can a hook fire another hook?</h3>
<p>None of the five action types takes another hook as its value, so there is nowhere in the settings to write "and then fire that hook".</p>
<p>But a hook fires when something calls a tool. What if the subagent a hook opens calls a tool itself: does the hook fire again?</p>
<p>The setup is one <code>PreToolUse</code> rule, matcher <code>Bash</code>, with two actions:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>command</code>: writes the command about to run into <code>ran.txt</code>, to count how many times the rule fires</li>
<li><code>agent</code>: opens a subagent and tells it to run <code>echo FROMHOOKAGENT</code> itself</li>
</ul>
<p>As settings:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{ </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"PreToolUse"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"matcher"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Bash"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"type"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"jq -r '</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">\"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">PreToolUse | </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">\"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> + .tool_input.command' >> ran.txt"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> },</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"type"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"agent"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"prompt"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Use the Bash tool to run exactly: echo FROMHOOKAGENT . Then return ok=true. $ARGUMENTS"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> }</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  ] }</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">] } }</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The <code>command</code> receives the hook input on stdin, pulls out <code>tool_input.command</code> (the command about to run) with <code>jq</code>, and appends it to <code>ran.txt</code>.</p>
<p>The main line calls Bash exactly once, running <code>echo MAIN</code>. Afterwards <code>ran.txt</code> has two lines:</p>
<pre><code>PreToolUse | echo MAIN
PreToolUse | echo FROMHOOKAGENT
</code></pre>
<p>The first line is the main line's call. The second is from the subagent the hook opened: when it called Bash, the engine checked the same <code>settings.json</code>, and <code>matcher: "Bash"</code> matched a second time.</p>
<p>The control changes one thing: the <code>agent</code> prompt becomes "reply with the single word OK, no commands needed", and <code>ran.txt</code> has only one line.</p>
<p>The two runs differ only in whether the model calls a tool. <strong>So for a hook to fire another hook, the subagent the hook opens has to call a tool itself.</strong></p>
<p>Why does it stop at two lines instead of firing forever?</p>
<p>Because on the second match, the engine ran only the <code>command</code> action and did not run the <code>agent</code> action again. In the <code>--debug-file</code> log, <code>Processing agent hook</code> appears only once. When the subagent the hook opened calls Bash, its <code>agent_id</code> is <code>hook-agent-…</code>; at that point the <code>command</code> hook fires as usual and the <code>agent</code> hook does not. Two runs of the same experiment gave the same result, and the official docs do not mention this.</p>
<p>Calls the engine makes itself do not fire hooks. An <code>mcp_tool</code> action has the engine call the MCP server directly; the server does receive it, but that <code>tools/call</code> never comes back round to <code>PreToolUse</code>.</p>
<h3>Can a hook call a skill?</h3>
<p>None of the five action types takes a skill name either. What is left is having the hook give the model a sentence asking it to make the call.</p>
<p>A hook script's output can include <code>additionalContext</code>, and the engine puts that text into the model's conversation. The script below is attached to <code>UserPromptSubmit</code>: every time the user sends a message, it tells the model to run the <code>greet</code> skill first:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">echo</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"You must now invoke the skill named greet using the Skill tool before answering."}}'</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>Registered in <code>settings.json</code> it looks like this. <code>UserPromptSubmit</code> does not compare tool names, so there is no matcher:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{ </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"UserPromptSubmit"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [{ </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"type"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"command"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"bash greet-hook.sh"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> }] }</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">] } }</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The <code>greet</code> skill's body only tells the model to reply <code>GREET-RAN</code>. Type <code>Say hello.</code> and the next step in the log is a <code>tool_use</code> named <code>Skill</code>, skill <code>greet</code>, ending at <code>GREET-RAN</code>.</p>
<p><strong>This route is not guaranteed.</strong> The hook only puts a sentence into the conversation; the model can follow it and call <code>Skill</code>, or ignore it.</p>
<h2>Which fields a skill wires through</h2>
<p><code>SKILL.md</code> frontmatter has three fields that wire to something else:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="yaml" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="yaml" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">name</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">example</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">description</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Example skill.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">allowed-tools</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Read</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">     # tool</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">context</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">fork</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">           # subagent</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">agent</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">probe</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">            # goes with context: fork, optional</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">hooks</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">:                  </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D"># hook</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">  PreToolUse</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">:</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    - </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">matcher</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Bash</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">      hooks</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">:</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">        - </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">type</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">command</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">          command</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">bash deny.sh</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">---</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>Write <code>context: fork</code> or <code>hooks</code> and the engine acts on it. <strong><code>allowed-tools</code>, on the other hand, restricts no tool.</strong></p>
<h3>Why does <code>Execute skill:</code> come back when the skill never ran?</h3>
<p>When the frontmatter has <code>allowed-tools</code>, <code>disallowed-tools</code> or <code>hooks</code>, the engine wants the user's approval before the <code>Skill</code> call goes through. Every experiment here runs under <code>-p</code>, where nobody can approve, so the engine refuses. Five skills, each with one extra field, invoked once each under <code>-p</code>:</p>





























<table><thead><tr><th>frontmatter adds</th><th><code>tool_result</code></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>(nothing)</td><td><code>Launching skill: inner</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>context: fork</code></td><td><code>Skill "forktest" completed (forked execution).</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>allowed-tools: Read</code></td><td><code>Execute skill: tooltest</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>disallowed-tools: Bash</code></td><td><code>Execute skill: dtest</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>hooks: PreToolUse …</code></td><td><code>Execute skill: hooktest</code></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><strong><code>Execute skill: &#x3C;name></code> is a refusal; the body of <code>SKILL.md</code> never loaded.</strong></p>
<p>Run the same <code>tooltest</code> in other modes and it is clear this step is waiting for approval:</p>
<ul>
<li>manual mode (asks the user every time): a dialog, "Use skill "tooltest"?"</li>
<li>auto mode (a classifier decides): lets it through</li>
<li><code>-p</code>: nobody can answer, so it is refused</li>
</ul>
<p>That is why the three experiments below also pass <code>--dangerously-skip-permissions</code> (allow every permission); without it the body never loads.</p>
<p>So which fields require approval? The binary holds a hardcoded list of fields that need no prompt (57 entries as of 2.1.302; <code>strings</code> finds it as <code>new Set(["type","progressMessage"…</code>). <code>hooks</code>, <code>allowed-tools</code> and <code>disallowed-tools</code> are not on it:</p>

























<table><thead><tr><th>frontmatter</th><th>asks first?</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>allowed-tools: Read</code></td><td>yes</td></tr><tr><td><code>allowed-tools: []</code></td><td>no, empty counts as not written</td></tr><tr><td><code>context: fork</code></td><td>no, it is on the list</td></tr><tr><td><code>foo: bar</code> (a key the engine does not know)</td><td>no</td></tr></tbody></table>
<h3>skill wires to a tool</h3>
<p><code>allowed-tools: Read</code> looks like "Read only". <code>restricttest</code> declares exactly that, and its body deliberately asks for Bash:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">name</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">restricttest</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">description</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Test skill. Use when the user says restricttest.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">allowed-tools</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Read</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Call the Bash tool with command: echo HELLO</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Then state in one line whether the Bash call succeeded or was refused.</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The binary describes the field as <code>Tools available to the model while this file is active</code> too. Typing <code>restricttest</code> each time and changing only the frontmatter:</p>





















<table><thead><tr><th>What the frontmatter declares</th><th>Does Bash run</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>no such line</td><td>it runs, <code>tool_result</code> comes back <code>HELLO</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>allowed-tools: Read</code></td><td>it runs, <code>tool_result</code> comes back <code>HELLO</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>disallowed-tools: Bash</code></td><td><code>Permission to use Bash has been denied.</code></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><strong><code>allowed-tools</code> only decides which tools run without asking the user; unlisted ones can still be called.</strong> <code>disallowed-tools</code> is what refuses, though Bash stays on the tool list and the engine refuses the call when it arrives. The restriction also lasts only for the turn the skill was called in: reopen the same conversation with <code>--resume</code>, send "run <code>echo AFTER</code>", and Bash comes back with <code>AFTER</code>.</p>
<h3>skill wires to a subagent</h3>
<p>A skill's body runs in the main line by default. Add <code>context: fork</code> and the engine opens a subagent to run it, handing only the result back to the main line:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="diff" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="diff" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  ---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  name: forktest</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  description: Test skill. Use when the user says forktest.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+ context: fork</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  ---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  Reply with exactly one word: FORKED</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>Called once each, <code>-</code> without it, <code>+</code> with it:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="diff" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="diff" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#FDAEB7;--shiki-light:#B31D28">- Launching skill: forktest</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+ Skill "forktest" completed (forked execution).</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+ Result:</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">+ FORKED</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p><code>agent</code> picks which agent type runs it: the name from a <code>.claude/agents/&#x3C;name>.md</code>, or a built-in type such as <code>Explore</code>. A name that does not exist raises nothing; the engine forks with general-purpose.</p>
<h3>skill wires to a hook</h3>
<p><code>hooktest</code> attaches a script that always denies Bash, and its body asks Bash to run <code>echo HELLO</code>:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">name</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">hooktest</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">description</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Test skill. Use when the user says hooktest.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">hooks</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">:</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">  PreToolUse</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">:</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    - </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">matcher</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Bash</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">      hooks</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">:</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">        - </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">type</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">command</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">          command</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">bash .claude/skills/hooktest/deny.sh</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Call the Bash tool with command: echo HELLO</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Then report in one line exactly what happened.</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>One line of JSON in <code>deny.sh</code> is enough:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">#!/bin/bash</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">echo</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK"}}'</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>On <code>deny</code> the engine never hands <code>echo HELLO</code> to the shell, and the model receives <code>PreToolUse:Bash hook error: BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK</code>.</p>
<p>Does the deny still apply after the skill finishes? Three messages go to one process (<code>claude -p --input-format stream-json</code>, each sent after the previous <code>result</code>), the first and last being plain commands unrelated to the skill:</p>

























<table><thead><tr><th>Input</th><th>What came back</th><th>Where things stand</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><code>echo BEFORE</code></td><td><code>BEFORE</code></td><td>the skill has not been invoked yet</td></tr><tr><td><code>hooktest</code></td><td><code>PreToolUse:Bash hook error: BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK</code></td><td>what got blocked is the body's <code>echo HELLO</code></td></tr><tr><td><code>echo AFTER</code></td><td><code>PreToolUse:Bash hook error: BLOCKED-BY-SKILL-HOOK</code></td><td>the skill has already finished</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p><strong>Once a skill has run, its <code>hooks:</code> stay on the process</strong>, and Bash after the skill is still refused. They go away only when the process exits; reopening the same session with <code>--resume</code> is already a new process, and <code>echo AFTER</code> comes back as <code>AFTER</code>.</p>
<p>Put the same rule in the <code>hooks:</code> of an agent definition at <code>.claude/agents/probe.md</code> and it applies only inside the subagent: probe running <code>echo SUB</code> gets <code>BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK</code>, and the main line's <code>echo AFTER</code> runs as usual. In an untrusted folder, <code>probe.md</code>'s <code>hooks:</code> are dropped wholesale while <code>SKILL.md</code>'s still register.</p>
<h3>skill wires to another skill</h3>
<p>No frontmatter field takes another skill's name, so the call has to go in the body:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="markdown" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">name</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">outer</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">description</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">Outer test skill. Use when the user says outer.</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">---</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">Invoke the skill named inner using the Skill tool. Then reply with whatever it returned.</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p><code>inner</code>'s body only tells the model to reply <code>INNER-RAN</code>. After typing <code>outer</code>, this happens in order:</p>
<pre><code>user: outer
→ the model calls Skill {"skill": "outer"}
→ the engine returns Launching skill: outer and loads outer's body
→ following outer's body, the model calls Skill {"skill": "inner"}
→ the engine returns Launching skill: inner and loads inner's body
→ following inner's body, the model replies INNER-RAN
</code></pre>
<p>Both calls come from the model. If the model does not follow <code>outer</code>'s body, <code>inner</code> never runs.</p>
<h2>Silent failures</h2>
<p>With each of the three settings below, a mistake raises no error from the engine and no hint in normal output; only the result differs from a correct setup.</p>
<p>The first two are typos:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="json" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">{ </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"PreToolUsee"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [ { </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"matcher"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"Bash"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">"hooks"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: [ </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#FDAEB7;--shiki-dark-font-style:italic;--shiki-light:#B31D28;--shiki-light-font-style:italic">...</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> ] } ] } }</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="yaml" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="yaml" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">context</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">fork</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-light:#22863A">agent</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">nosuchagent</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The third has nothing misspelled: the folder holding <code>.claude/agents/probe.md</code> has simply never been trusted.</p>
<p><strong>So to catch these, the only way is to list what a correct setup should produce, then check whether it appeared.</strong></p>





























<table><thead><tr><th>What is wrong</th><th>What shows up when correct</th><th>What the wrong one shows</th><th>Any hint</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>event name <code>PreToolUsee</code> in <code>settings.json</code>, one e too many</td><td><code>--include-hook-events</code> adds <code>hook_started</code> and <code>hook_response</code></td><td>neither appears, Bash runs anyway</td><td>nothing in <code>--include-hook-events</code> (hook events in stream-json). Only <code>--debug</code> (debug log on stderr) prints <code>Unknown hook event "PreToolUsee" was ignored</code> (settings file loaded through <code>--settings</code>)</td></tr><tr><td><code>agent: nosuchagent</code> on a skill</td><td><code>agent: mycustom</code> returns <code>CUSTOM: FORKED</code></td><td>returns <code>FORKED</code>, forking with general-purpose</td><td>none</td></tr><tr><td>folder not trusted</td><td><code>deny.sh</code> gets its own <code>hook_started</code> and <code>hook_response</code>, <code>echo SUB</code> returns <code>BLOCKED-BY-AGENT-HOOK</code></td><td>no events at all, <code>echo SUB</code> returns <code>SUB</code>; the <code>hooks:</code> in the agent's frontmatter are dropped wholesale</td><td><code>-p</code> never shows the trust dialog. Only <code>--debug</code> prints <code>Skipping frontmatter hooks for agent '…': the folder its definition file came from is not trusted</code></td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>Trust is asked once per folder: the first interactive session started there puts up a dialog asking whether to trust it, and the answer is stored as <code>hasTrustDialogAccepted</code> in <code>~/.claude.json</code>. Under <code>-p</code> that dialog never appears.</p>
<h2>caveat</h2>
<p>The CLI and the SDK execute the same binary; <code>shasum</code> matches. The SDK can also take <code>agents</code>, <code>mcpServers</code> and hook callbacks straight as options; <code>tools</code> and <code>skills</code> behave differently in <code>query()</code>, see the <code>query()</code> table above.</p>
<p>Every measurement in this article ran with <code>-p</code>, and <code>-p</code> changes two results:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>tooltest</code> returns <code>Execute skill: tooltest</code>, because under <code>-p</code> nobody answers the approval prompt</li>
<li><code>forktest</code>'s result comes straight back to the main line, because <code>-p</code> does not push the subagent into the background</li>
</ul>
<p>The same two skills, rerun in the other two modes. How each mode starts:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="bash" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">claude</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5"> --permission-mode</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> manual</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">   # manual mode</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">claude</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">                            # default auto mode</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">claude</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5"> -p</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> "tooltest"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">              # -p</span></span></code></pre></figure>
